title: openai-compat: propagate tool selection confidence and resume fragmented tool streams
author: Ravi Singh
release_notes: Added tool_choice confidence propagation, deterministic tie-breaker for tool selection, resume tokens for partial tool streams, and enhanced schema mapping for union/optional fields in OpenAI compatibility layer. Backwards compatible for most consumers; small clients that relied on exact event framing should upgrade to handle resume envelopes.
description: Motivation: Our OpenAI compatibility layer has seen multiple edge cases in production where tool/function calls returned fragmented streaming outputs or non-deterministic tool_choice picks in ambiguous situations. This caused flaky integrations in customers' function-call handlers and complicated observability for reruns. This PR introduces three focused changes: 1) carry a tool_choice_confidence metric across the compat layer and expose a deterministic tie-breaker when confidences are equal, 2) introduce resume envelopes/tokens for fragmented tool response streams so client SDKs can reassemble or resume partial tool outputs without losing alignment, and 3) enhance the tool schema mapping to better support union types and optional properties when translating OpenAI-style function schemas to our internal tool descriptors. Changeset summary: - API: openai-compat adapter now emits an additional field in tool pick events: "tool_choice_confidence" (0.0-1.0) and a canonical "tool_choice_resolver" header when a deterministic tie-breaker was used. - Streaming: tool stream fragments now include resume_token in stream envelopes; the compat adapter can accept a resume_token header to continue a previously interrupted tool stream. We added resume token generation and validation logic to the runtime. - Schema mapping: mapper now supports union arrays (e.g., [string, object]) by producing a typed-choice property in the internal schema and marks optional fields explicitly to preserve OpenAI "optional" semantics. - SDKs: Python and TypeScript OpenAI compatibility helpers updated to surface confidence and resume tokens to callers and to stitch fragmented messages into a single tool invocation response. - Tests: integration tests for resume flows, deterministic tie-breaker, and schema union mapping. - Docs: openai-compat.md updated with migration notes and examples for reading tool_choice_confidence and using resume tokens. Checklist: - [x] design doc and Linear tickets (ENG-1284) - [x] unit tests added for mapper and stream resume logic - [x] integration tests for SDK rehydration flows - [x] docs updated with example usage and migration guidance - [x] feature gated behind compat.v1.tool_choice_confidence for staged rollout Commits (high-level): - feat(openai-compat): add tool_choice_confidence to pick events - feat(runtime): resume token generation and validation for tool streams - feat(mapper): support union types and optional fields in schema mapping - refactor(sdk/python): expose resume_token and merge helper in compat client - test(integration): add resume stream and tie-breaker tests - docs: openai-compat migration and examples Examples of changed files (high-level paths): - api/openai/compat/adapter.go - runtime/stream/resume_manager.go - runtime/tool/router.go - runtime/tool/selector.go - pkg/schema/mapper.go - sdk/python/redwood_openai_compat.py - sdk/typescript/openaiCompat.ts - tests/integration/test_tool_resume_flow.go - docs/openai-compat.md Small illustrative snippets (kept short): - In adapter.go: "event.ToolPick.Confidence = toolChoiceConfidence" - In resume_manager.go: "if incoming.ResumeToken != nil { validateAndAppend(incoming) } else { startNewStream() }" Review discussion (condensed): - Ava Patel (review): "Neat approach. Main concern: exposing confidence to users may cause them to rely on it for correctness. Can we make it explicit in docs that confidence is advisory and not a binary correctness signal?" - Author (Ravi): "Agree, added explicit wording in docs and returned an example how to fallback to our deterministic tie-breaker header. Also added feature gate for orgs to opt-in while we gather metrics." - Michael Chen (review): "resume token validation looks good but edge case: what happens if token TTL expires mid-stream? We should return a clear HTTP 410 with a well-documented recovery path." - Author: "Added 410 handling and a small helper in SDKs that will retry a fresh invocation automatically when token is expired. Tests added." - Lina Gómez (review): "Mapper change LGTM; please ensure it won't explode on deeply nested unions. Suggest adding a depth cap and transform to flat-choice entries." - Author: "Added a depth cap of 6 and additional unit tests for nested unions. Mapper will fall back to raw object when depth exceeded." CI & flaky test notes: - CI initially failed on integration test test_tool_resume_flow due to a timing race in the mock stream harness. I reran the job and it passed on the second attempt. All other checks (lint, unit tests, contract tests) passed. Migration notes for customers: - Existing consumers should continue to work. To observe the new fields, upgrade to compat v1 clients or opt into the feature gate. - SDKs will surface resume_token in stream events; if clients ignore it they will keep functioning but cannot resume partial tool streams. - Clients that parsed event boundaries strictly should update to accept resume envelopes as part of the stream (examples in docs). Operational considerations: - We added logging at INFO level when deterministic tie-breakers are used and at WARN when resume tokens are retried more than 3 times. This will help debug integration issues without spamming logs. Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind compat.v1.tool_choice_confidence for first 2 weeks in hosted stable, then enable by default with a 24h observability window. - Monitor: streaming error rate, resume token replays, and customer-reported function failures. Notes for support: SUP-4421 reference contains a sample payload from the customer that triggered the change; attaching the sample to the Linear ticket. Merge outcome: Squashed into a single commit and merged to main. No follow-up PRs required; post-merge tasks include enabling feature gate in the beta orgs and a short announcement in the developer changelog.
